=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible paired leaves attached at the same node along the stem in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear concentrated near the shoot tip and lower nodes)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided single blades)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth and continuous)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (widest near the middle with tapering ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapers to a distinct, elongated point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapers gradually to the petiole attachment)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with veins branching laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, moderately spaced, curving towards the apex (percurrent)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous, slightly glossy (smooth texture with a slight sheen)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are clearly visible but relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (cylindrical and rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid and brownish, typical of a seedling tree)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent
    19. Stem color: brown (visible on the main stem and petioles)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no obvious ridges or lenticels visible)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Some leaves exhibit marginal holes and dark blotches; these are described neutrally as damage without inferring cause. The background shows a forest floor covered in leaf litter.
